conbody.p: Reviewing commits helps you understand how the work done on a branch changes the project itself. This helps you build a mental model of how the work done on multiple branches affects the project.
This mental model is useful when performing merge-like operations between branches and helps prevent merge conflicts.
Review commits on Git History or in an external application of your choice.

section.title: Review commits on Git History
section.p: The Git History table lists commits in order from latest to oldest.
Select a commit to view details about it on the bottom-left Commit details pane and the resources it modifies on the bottom-right Affected resources pane .
Select multiple revisions to view what changed between the latest and oldest selected commit. The Git History view lists the selected commits on the bottom-left Commit details pane.
The bottom-right Affected resources pane lists the files modified after the oldest commit.
If you have uncommitted changes on your working copy,
Compare your working copy against another revision to view differences between the working copy and that revision.
